title: Air India, IndiGo and Lufthansa Suspend Riyadh Flights After Houthi Missile Strike on Airport
excerpt: Nearly half of all departures from Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport were cancelled Thursday as airlines pulled out after Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on the Saudi capital's airport.
body:
• Lufthansa Group suspended all Riyadh flights through October 16, while Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa Air cancelled services through October 9-10 after the Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on King Khalid International Airport.
  • Aviation data firm Cirium recorded 49.7% of Riyadh departures cancelled by Thursday afternoon, with dozens more international flights scrubbed across Saudi airports.
  • If you are flying to Riyadh this week: check your flight status before heading to the airport. IndiGo, Air India, Air India Express and Akasa are offering free rescheduling or full refunds to affected passengers.
  • The Indian Embassy in Riyadh has advised nationals in Saudi Arabia to stay alert, remain indoors if needed, and avoid circulating videos of the attacks.

Lufthansa Group and three Indian airlines suspended all flights to Riyadh on Thursday after Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on the Saudi capital's airport, a sharp escalation that threw Gulf aviation into chaos and stranded thousands of travellers.

A Lufthansa spokesperson told Reuters the German group's airlines would halt Riyadh services through October 16, citing "current developments in the Middle East." Air India and Air India Express cancelled all flights to and from the Saudi capital until October 10, while IndiGo cancelled its Riyadh services until October 9 and Akasa Air suspended its flights until October 10. Smoke was seen rising from a stationary aircraft at Riyadh airport earlier on Thursday, according to a witness account reported by Reuters.

An unprecedented aviation shutdown

"Aviation data firm Cirium recorded 49.7% of Riyadh departures cancelled by Thursday afternoon, with dozens more international flights scrubbed across Saudi airports."

The scale of the disruption is remarkable. Data from aviation analytics firm Cirium showed 49.7% of scheduled departures from Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport had been cancelled by Thursday afternoon, with another 31 cancellations expected across Saudi airports on Friday. Flight tracker FlightRadar24 recorded dozens of international flights bound for Riyadh being scrapped on Thursday evening, as the Houthis renewed explicit threats against airlines operating in Saudi airspace — warning carriers that any aircraft flying over the kingdom, apart from routes to Mecca and Medina, could be considered a target.

The Houthis said they had struck King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the claim, but officials said three people had been killed this week in strikes on the Riyadh and Abha airports.

Indian carriers scramble

The impact on Indian carriers was immediate and severe. An Air India flight from Delhi to Riyadh, AI2243, turned back to the Indian capital mid-journey on Thursday and the service was subsequently cancelled. Air India operates seven weekly flights to Riyadh from Delhi and Mumbai, while Air India Express runs 16 weekly services from Bengaluru, Kochi, Kannur and Kozhikode. IndiGo diverted a Hyderabad–Riyadh aircraft to Dammam and cancelled its Friday departures from Mumbai, Delhi and Hyderabad.

All four Indian carriers told passengers they could rebook at no charge or take full refunds. "Given the prevailing security situation in the region, IndiGo has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh until 09 October 2026," the airline said in a statement, adding it was proactively contacting affected passengers. Air India Express advised guests to expect complimentary rescheduling or a full refund on cancellation, while Akasa Air said it was monitoring the situation in real time.

What it means for the diaspora

Saudi Arabia is home to one of the world's largest Indian expatriate populations — roughly 2.5 million people, many of them blue-collar workers and professionals whose families depend on regular home visits. The cancellations come just as many were finalising travel plans around the festive season. For passengers with non-refundable connecting itineraries, travel insurance claims may apply where trip disruption is covered.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh issued an advisory urging all Indian nationals in the kingdom to remain alert, stay indoors if necessary, follow instructions from local authorities, and refrain from recording or circulating videos of the attacks.

What to watch

The key question now is duration. Lufthansa's suspension through October 16 suggests carriers expect the threat to persist for at least a week. Whether Gulf carriers like Emirates, Qatar Airways and Saudia follow the European and Indian airlines in suspending service will determine whether Riyadh becomes effectively cut off from international air travel. Travellers booked to Saudi Arabia in the coming days should check their airline's advisories before departing and keep alternative routings — via Dammam or Jeddah — in view.
